task: Review completed runs and report what actually went wrong, not what plausibly could. Use this bounded initial evidence pass: (1) begin with the intermediate program (runs/list-runs 20 nil) exactly as written, without wrapping it in return; (2) choose one candidate run and call (runs/review-seed run-id). That one PTC-Lisp function performs three distinct audited source reads and returns the run's filtered error events, final exact generated program, and final exact model response with their snapshot identities. It deliberately omits the cumulative request transcript to keep the initial observation small. After those two observations, return the final report unless one specifically named fact required by the result schema is still missing. (runs/provenance run-id) identifies component replacements. (runs/effective-prelude run-id component-id) returns the source actually executed by that run; repository tools return the current workspace source. Compare their identities when historical behavior depends on a component. You may make at most one targeted follow-up call: use runs/latest-model-exchange for the complete final request transcript, runs/capability-calls for exact tool data, runs/effective-prelude for compiled code, or runs/provider-exchanges for provider wire evidence. Otherwise recommend "gather-more-evidence" and name the missing fact. Do not open unfiltered turn pages, do not traverse older generated-source or model-exchange pages, and do not mechanically exhaust a cursor in this review task. Treat every runs/* or repo/* result as an intermediate observation and never return it directly; use return only for the final schema-shaped report. Return a JSON object with "summary", "findings", "recommended_next_action", and "rationale". A finding must cite the run and event evidence it rests on. Every evidence item has exactly four string-keyed fields: "provider", "snapshot_hash", "resource", and "positions". Copy provider and snapshot_hash from the source result. For history or private-history, resource is the run ID and positions contains positive event sequence IDs. For workspace, resource is the relative path and positions contains the positive source line numbers cited. Report a finding seen in exactly one run with occurrences 1 rather than describing it as a pattern. If the runs show no reusable problem, recommend "no-action" and say why. Every paged collection accepts nil for the first page and only an exact returned next_cursor afterwards; never invent or transform a cursor.
